Copilot inside Word/Excel/PowerPoint/OneNote now needs the paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence (change rolled out April–May 2026).
Power BI: Copilot needs Fabric F64+ or a Copilot capacity; Pro alone doesn't include it.

apps.name: Word
apps.sub: Letters, SOPs, mail merge, formal documents

apps.name: Power Query
apps.sub: Inside Excel (Data › Get Data) and Power BI. Clean and combine data with clicks

apps.name: Power BI
apps.sub: Interactive dashboards for management. Pro licence needed to share

apps.name: Power Apps
apps.sub: Simple phone/PC forms and apps on top of your data

apps.sub: Trackers and logs with audit trail

apps.sub: Live tables and lists inside chats and emails

apps.sub: AI assistant. Free Chat vs paid in-app Copilot

features.name: Styles + Navigation pane
features.what: Apply Heading 1/2 styles instead of manual bold. The Navigation pane (Ctrl+F) then becomes a clickable outline, and you restyle the whole document in one click.
features.use: Month-end closing SOP or accounting policy manual you can jump around in.
steps: Click a heading line › Home › Heading 1
Subheadings › Heading 2
Ctrl+F opens the Navigation pane; drag headings to reorder sections
Right-click Heading 1 › Modify to change every heading at once
features.plain: Styles are saved formats like 'Heading 1'. Word remembers which lines are headings, so it can build an outline and change all of them together.
features.example: You type 'Section 3: Accruals' and click Heading 1. It now shows in the Navigation pane. Click it there and Word jumps to that section.
features.watch: Making a line bold and big by hand is NOT a heading. Word can't see it, so it won't show in the outline or the table of contents.

features.name: Auto table of contents, captions & cross-references
features.what: References › Table of Contents builds from your headings. Captions number tables/figures; cross-references update when numbering changes.
features.use: Audit pack index; board paper that says 'see Table 3' and stays right after edits.
features.where: References › Table of Contents · Insert Caption · Cross-reference
steps: Apply heading styles first
References › Table of Contents › Automatic Table 1
Select a table › References › Insert Caption › Label: Table
Where you mention it: References › Cross-reference › Table › Only label and number
Before printing: Ctrl+A, then F9 to update everything
features.plain: Word writes the contents page and table numbers for you, and keeps them correct when pages move.
features.example: Insert a table between Table 2 and Table 3. Press F9: the old Table 3 becomes Table 4, and every 'see Table 4' in the text updates too.
features.watch: It doesn't update by itself. Always select all and press F9 before printing or sending.

features.name: Mail Merge from Excel
features.what: Mailings › Start Mail Merge. One letter template + Excel list = one letter (or email) per row with its own name and amount.
features.use: Debtor balance confirmation letters for all customers; overdue reminders; supplier statements. Format amounts with the field switch \# "#,##0.00".
steps: In Excel, put headers in row 1 (Name, Address, Balance), one customer per row
Word › Mailings › Select Recipients › Use an Existing List › pick the sheet
Insert Merge Field wherever each value goes
Preview Results and check a few letters
Finish & Merge › Edit Individual Documents, or Send Email Messages
features.plain: Write one letter with blanks. Word fills the blanks from an Excel list and makes one letter per row.
features.example: Excel: Ali Sdn Bhd | 12,500.00. Letter: 'Dear «Name», your balance is RM«Balance».' Result: 'Dear Ali Sdn Bhd, your balance is RM12,500.00.'
features.watch: Amounts may come out as 12500.1 with no commas. Fix it with the number format field switch, or format the column as text in Excel first.

features.name: Templates (.dotx) & Quick Parts
features.what: Save a letterhead as a template; save signature blocks, standard clauses and addresses as Quick Parts to insert with two keystrokes.
features.use: Standard supplier letter, payment voucher cover, bank instruction letter layout.
features.where: File › Save As › Word Template · Insert › Quick Parts
steps: Build the letterhead once › Save As › Word Template (.dotx)
File › New › Personal to start a letter from it
Select a signature block › Insert › Quick Parts › Save Selection to Quick Part Gallery
Next time type the Quick Part name and press F3
features.plain: A template is a blank starting file you reuse without overwriting it. Quick Parts are saved text blocks you insert in seconds.
features.example: Save your letterhead as 'Supplier Letter.dotx'. File › New gives you a fresh copy each time; the template itself never changes.
features.watch: Opening the .dotx file directly edits the template. Use File › New › Personal instead.

features.name: Track Changes & Compare Documents
features.what: Review › Track Changes records every edit. Review › Compare shows differences between two versions even if nobody tracked.
features.use: Review service agreement with legal; compare policy v3 vs v4 before approval.
steps: Turn on Track Changes (Ctrl+Shift+E) before sending for review
Edits show in colour; Accept or Reject one by one
No tracking used? Review › Compare › Compare › pick Original and Revised › OK
features.plain: Track Changes records every edit in colour so you can accept or reject each one. Compare finds the differences between two versions for you.
features.example: Legal changes '30 days' to '45 days'. You see '30' crossed out and '45' in colour, and you click Accept or Reject.
features.watch: Accepting all changes removes the history. Keep a copy of the tracked version for your records.

features.name: Fill-in forms (content controls + Restrict Editing)
features.what: Developer tab › drop-downs, date pickers, check boxes. Restrict Editing so people can only type in the blanks.
features.use: Vendor registration form, petty cash claim form, new GL account request.
features.oldVersion: Content controls look like plain text in very old Word (2007 and before).
features.where: File › Options › Customize Ribbon › tick Developer · Developer › Controls
steps: Show the Developer tab
Insert Drop-Down List, Date Picker or Check Box where the blanks go
Properties › add the choices
Review › Restrict Editing › Filling in forms › Yes, Start Enforcing Protection
features.plain: A form where people can only fill in the blanks and can't change your wording or layout.
features.example: A claim form with a drop-down for Department, a date picker for Date and a box for Amount. Everything else is locked.
features.watch: Turn on Restrict Editing last. While it's on, you can't edit the form either; stop protection first.

features.name: Sections, landscape pages & different headers
features.what: Layout › Breaks › Next Page lets one page be landscape and gives each part its own header/footer and page numbering.
features.use: Report with a wide landscape schedule in the middle; appendix numbered A-1, A-2.
features.where: Layout › Breaks › Next Page · Layout › Orientation
steps: Cursor before the wide table › Breaks › Next Page
Do the same after the table
Click in the middle section › Orientation › Landscape
Double-click the header › untick Link to Previous to give it its own header
features.plain: A section break splits the document, so one part can have different page orientation, headers or page numbers.
features.example: Pages 1–4 portrait, page 5 a wide landscape ageing table, pages 6–8 back to portrait.
features.watch: A Page Break isn't a Section Break. Only Layout › Breaks › Next Page lets you change orientation for one part.

features.name: Paste Link from Excel
features.what: Copy in Excel › Paste Special › Paste link. Numbers in Word update when the Excel file changes.
features.use: Monthly management commentary where the numbers come from the forecast workbook.
features.oldVersion: Links break if the file moves or goes to someone else. Break links on the copy you send.
features.where: Excel: Copy · Word: Home › Paste › Paste Special › Paste link
steps: Copy the range or chart in Excel
Word › Paste Special › Paste link › Microsoft Excel Worksheet Object
After Excel changes: right-click › Update Link
Before sending: File › Info › Edit Links to Files › Break Link
features.plain: Paste numbers from Excel that stay connected, so the Word report updates when the Excel file changes.
features.example: Excel shows Revenue 1,250. You change it to 1,300; in Word, right-click › Update Link and it shows 1,300.
features.watch: If you rename or move the Excel file, the link breaks. Keep both files in the same folder.

features.name: Open & edit PDF in Word
features.what: Open a PDF directly in Word and it converts to editable text (layout may shift).
features.use: Re-use wording from a bank or auditor letter that only came as PDF.
steps: Open the PDF from Word and click OK on the conversion message
Check the layout and copy what you need
Keep the original PDF as the record
features.plain: Word can turn a PDF into an editable Word document, so you don't retype it.
features.example: Open the bank's PDF letter in Word, copy the paragraph you need, and paste it into your reply.
features.watch: Tables and columns may shift. Check the numbers against the original PDF.

features.name: Dictate & Transcribe
features.what: Home › Dictate types as you speak. Transcribe (Word for web) turns a recording into text with speakers.
features.use: Draft meeting minutes quickly; dictate long explanations for variance notes.
features.it: Uses Microsoft cloud speech service ('connected experiences'); IT can turn it off for privacy.
features.where: Home › Dictate · Word for web: Home › Dictate ▾ › Transcribe
steps: Click Dictate and allow the microphone
Say punctuation out loud: 'comma', 'full stop', 'new line'
For a recording: Word for web › Transcribe › Upload audio › Add to document
features.plain: Speak and Word types for you (Dictate), or upload a recording and Word turns it into text (Transcribe).
features.example: Say 'The variance is due to higher freight cost full stop'. Word types: 'The variance is due to higher freight cost.'
features.watch: Numbers and names often come out wrong. Always proofread.

features.name: Editor & Translate
features.what: Grammar/clarity checks and Review › Translate for a selection or whole document.
features.use: Rough translation to read a memo in another language; polish English for management reviewers. Always get a human check for formal use.
features.it: Text is sent to Microsoft translation service; IT may disable for confidential documents.
steps: Home › Editor shows a score and suggestions
Select text › Review › Translate › Translate Selection
Choose the language › Insert
Ask a fluent person to check before formal use
features.plain: Editor checks spelling, grammar and clarity. Translate turns text into another language inside Word.
features.example: Select a paragraph › Translate › Japanese. The translation appears on the right, ready to insert.
features.watch: Machine translation can be wrong in tone or meaning. Use it to understand; get a person to check formal letters.

features.name: Sensitivity labels
features.what: Mark a document Confidential/Internal; some labels also encrypt and add a watermark.
features.use: Salary review, payroll summary, board minutes.
features.it: Configured only by IT (Microsoft Purview). If you don't see it, the company hasn't enabled it.
features.oldVersion: Encrypted files may not open in old Office or outside the company.
features.where: Home › Sensitivity (or File › Info › Protect Document)
steps: Look for the Sensitivity button on the Home tab
Pick a label such as Confidential
The label may add a header, watermark and encryption automatically
features.plain: A tag like 'Confidential' that marks how sensitive a file is, and can lock it so only staff can open it.
features.example: Label the salary file 'Confidential'. A watermark appears, and it won't open for people outside the company.
features.watch: You only see this if IT has set it up. You can't create labels yourself.

features.name: Word table formulas & fields
features.what: Insert › Quick Parts › Field, or Layout › Formula in a table (=SUM(ABOVE)). Press F9 to update.
features.use: Simple totals in a Word quotation or claim form without Excel.
features.where: Table Layout › Formula · Insert › Quick Parts › Field
steps: Click the total cell in a Word table
Layout › Formula › =SUM(ABOVE)
Number format: #,##0.00
After changing numbers: Ctrl+A, then F9
features.plain: Word tables can do simple sums, so totals in a Word form calculate themselves.
features.example: A column with 100, 250, 50. In the total cell: =SUM(ABOVE) gives 400.
features.watch: It doesn't recalculate live like Excel. Press F9 after changing numbers.

features.name: Word macros (VBA)
features.what: Record or write VBA to repeat formatting or loop files.
features.use: Batch convert a folder of letters to PDF; clean up SAP text exports pasted into Word.
features.it: Macros in files from email/internet are blocked by default; IT may allow only signed macros or trusted folders.
features.oldVersion: Must save as .docm; Word for web and mobile can't run them.
features.where: View › Macros › Record Macro · Alt+F11 to see code
steps: Record the steps once
Alt+F11 and read the recorded code
Save as .docm
Run with Alt+F8
features.plain: A macro is a recorded set of steps you can replay with one click, or code that repeats a task many times.
features.example: Record: Save As PDF. Then a short loop runs it on 50 letters in a folder, saving 50 PDFs.
features.watch: Files with macros from email are blocked by default. Keep macros in your own trusted files.

features.name: Excel Tables (Ctrl+T)
features.what: Turns a range into a Table: auto-expands, keeps formulas consistent, gives names like Sales[Amount]. Pivots and Power Query love Tables.
features.use: AP invoice listing or accrual schedule that grows every month without fixing ranges.
steps: Click any cell in your data › Ctrl+T › tick My table has headers
Table Design › Table Name › rename, e.g. tblAP
Type a new row under the table: it joins and formulas copy down
Use the name in formulas: =SUM(tblAP[Amount])
features.plain: Turns a block of data into a smart list that grows by itself, with filters and named columns.
features.example: Rows A1:E100. After Ctrl+T, typing in row 101 adds it to the table, and =SUM(tblAP[Amount]) includes it automatically.
features.watch: Don't leave blank rows or columns inside the data before pressing Ctrl+T.

features.name: Custom number formats
features.what: Ctrl+1 › Custom. #,##0;(#,##0);"-" shows negatives in brackets and zero as dash. #,##0, shows thousands without dividing.
features.use: P&L in RM'000 with brackets, ready for management reviewers, while the cell still holds the full number.
steps: Select the amounts › Ctrl+1 › Custom
The cell keeps the full number; only the display changes
features.plain: Change how a number looks without changing its value: brackets for negatives, a dash for zero, thousands.
features.example: -12345 shows as (12,345); 0 shows as -; with #,##0, then 1,250,000 shows as 1,250.
features.watch: It's display only. The cell still holds 1,250,000, so formulas use the full number.

features.name: Paste Special tricks
features.what: Values only, Transpose, Skip blanks, and Multiply: type -1, copy, Paste Special › Multiply to flip signs.
features.use: Flip SAP credit-side signs in one go; freeze a forecast as values before sending.
steps: Type -1 in a blank cell and copy it
Select the amounts › Ctrl+Alt+V › Multiply › OK
Values only: Ctrl+Alt+V › Values
Turn rows into columns: tick Transpose
features.plain: Paste only part of what you copied (just values or formats), or do maths while pasting.
features.example: SAP gives credits as positive. Copy -1 › select the amounts › Paste Special › Multiply: 500 becomes -500.
features.watch: Paste Values removes the formulas. Do it on a copy if you still need them.

features.name: Go To Special: fill the blanks
features.what: Ctrl+G › Special › Blanks, type = and the cell above, Ctrl+Enter. Then paste as values.
features.use: SAP reports that print company code only once per group; fill it down for every row.
features.where: Home › Find & Select › Go To Special
steps: Select the column › Ctrl+G › Special › Blanks
Type = then press the ↑ arrow key
Press Ctrl+Enter to fill every blank
Copy the column › Paste values
features.plain: Select only the empty cells at once and fill each with the value above it.
features.watch: Paste as values afterwards, or the cells keep '=A2' formulas that break when you sort.

features.name: Text to Columns & Flash Fill
features.what: Split one column by delimiter; fix text dates. Flash Fill (Ctrl+E) copies a pattern you type once.
features.use: SAP dates exported as 31.10.2026 text; split 'GL - Description'; extract invoice number.
features.where: Data › Text to Columns · Data › Flash Fill (Ctrl+E)
steps: Select the column › Text to Columns › Delimited › choose the separator
For text dates: last step › Column data format › Date › DMY
Flash Fill: type the result for row 1, move down, press Ctrl+E
features.plain: Split one column into several, or fix text that should be dates. Flash Fill copies a pattern you show it once.
features.example: '400100 - Freight' becomes 400100 | Freight. The text '31.10.2026' becomes a real date you can sort.
features.watch: Dates can turn into the wrong month. Choose DMY in the last step.

features.name: Data validation drop-downs
features.what: Data › Data Validation › List. Restricts input to your list.
features.use: Cost centre, company code, status (Open/Pending HOD/Closed) in shared templates.
steps: Keep the list in a Table on a 'Lists' sheet
Select input cells › Data Validation › Allow: List
Source: select the list range
Error Alert tab › Style: Stop
features.plain: Limit a cell to choices from a list, so people can't type wrong or different spellings.
features.example: The Status cell offers only Open, Pending HOD, Closed. Typing 'done' gives an error.
features.watch: Pasting over the cell removes the rule. Ask users to type or pick, not paste.

features.name: Conditional formatting
features.what: Colour cells by rules, data bars, icon sets, or a formula.
features.use: Highlight AR > 90 days, variances > 10%, duplicates in invoice numbers.
steps: Turn on Background color › fx
Choose Rules, or Field value with a colour measure
Example: Colour = IF([DSO] > 60, "#C0392B", "#1E8E5A")
features.plain: Colour numbers automatically by rules, so good and bad stand out.
features.example: DSO 72 turns red (target 60); 45 turns green.
features.watch: Rules on percentages use decimals (0.6), not 60.

features.name: SUMIFS / COUNTIFS / AVERAGEIFS
features.what: Sum or count with several conditions.
features.use: Sum GL amount by company code + account + fiscal month from a raw SAP dump.
steps: Pattern: =SUMIFS(sum_range, criteria_range1, criteria1, …)
Example: =SUMIFS(tblGL[Amount], tblGL[CoCode], $A2, tblGL[Period], B$1)
Lock with $ so it copies across a grid
features.plain: Add up (or count) only the rows that meet your conditions.
features.example: =SUMIFS(Amount, CoCode, "1000", Month, "Oct") adds only company 1000's October amounts.
features.watch: Text numbers don't match real numbers. '1000' as text won't match 1000 as a number.

features.name: XLOOKUP
features.what: Modern lookup: any direction, built-in 'if not found', exact by default, can return several columns.
features.use: Pull vendor name from vendor master; last match by date; exchange rate by date with approximate match.
features.oldVersion: Excel 2019 and older show #NAME? when they recalculate. Use INDEX+MATCH for files going to old Excel.
steps: =XLOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_array, return_array, "Not found")
Return several columns: select them all as return_array
Last match: add match mode 0 and search mode -1
features.plain: Find a value in one list and bring back related information. It's the modern, easier VLOOKUP.
features.example: =XLOOKUP("V001", VendorID, VendorName, "Not found") returns 'ABC Supplies'.
features.watch: Shows #NAME? in Excel 2019 and older. Use INDEX+MATCH if the file goes to old Excel.

features.name: INDEX + MATCH
features.what: The classic two-way lookup. Works in every version.
features.use: Files sent to external auditors or subsidiaries with unknown Excel versions.
steps: =INDEX(return_column, MATCH(lookup_value, lookup_column, 0))
Two-way: =INDEX(table, MATCH(row_value, row_list, 0), MATCH(col_value, col_list, 0))
Always keep the 0 for exact match
features.plain: Two functions that together do a lookup. MATCH finds the row number, INDEX picks the value from that row.
features.example: MATCH("V001", IDs, 0) → 3. INDEX(Names, 3) → 'ABC Supplies'.
features.watch: Forget the 0 in MATCH and it may return a wrong 'close' match.

features.name: Fiscal-year date formulas
features.what: EOMONTH, EDATE, TODAY. Fiscal period for Apr–Mar: =MOD(MONTH(A2)-4,12)+1. FY start year: =YEAR(A2)-(MONTH(A2)<4).
features.use: Map SAP posting dates to P1–P12; ageing days =TODAY()-DueDate; month-end accrual dates.
steps: Fiscal period (April = 1): =MOD(MONTH(A2)-4,12)+1
Fiscal year label: ="FY"&(YEAR(A2)-(MONTH(A2)<4))
Month-end: =EOMONTH(A2,0)
Ageing days: =TODAY()-DueDate
features.plain: Formulas that turn a date into your fiscal month and year when the year starts in April.
features.example: 15 May 2026 → period 2, FY2026. 10 Feb 2027 → period 11, FY2026.
features.watch: Check that the cell holds a real date (right-aligned), not text.

features.name: ROUND & precision control
features.what: ROUND(x,2) at the right step so totals match. Avoid 'Set precision as displayed' (it changes data permanently).
features.use: Stop RM0.01 differences between your schedule and SAP.
steps: Round at line level: =ROUND(A2*rate,2)
Decide: sum of rounded lines or rounded total, whichever matches the system
Check: =SUM(range)-SystemTotal should be 0
features.plain: Round at the right step so your totals match the system to the cent.
features.example: Ten lines of 33.333 add to 333.33, but rounded lines (33.33 × 10) add to 333.30. Decide which one SAP uses.
features.watch: Formatting to 2 decimals only hides the decimals. It doesn't round the value.

features.name: IFERROR, IFS, SWITCH
features.what: Cleaner logic. IFS checks several conditions; SWITCH maps codes to labels.
features.use: Map company codes to company names; ageing buckets 0-30/31-60/61-90/>90.
features.oldVersion: IFS/SWITCH show #NAME? in 2016.
steps: =IFERROR(XLOOKUP(…),0)
=SWITCH(A2,"1000","Company A","2000","Company B","Other")
features.plain: Cleaner if-then logic. IFERROR replaces errors, IFS checks several conditions, SWITCH maps codes to names.
features.watch: IFERROR hides real mistakes too. Use it only where an error is expected.

features.name: Dynamic arrays: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE
features.what: One formula spills a whole list that updates itself.
features.use: Live list of unpaid invoices for the vendor typed in a cell; unique customer list for a dropdown.
features.oldVersion: 2019 and older: #NAME? or a frozen legacy array.
features.where: Type in one cell; it spills
steps: =FILTER(tblAP, (tblAP[Vendor]=H1)*(tblAP[Status]="Open"))
=SORT(UNIQUE(tblAR[Customer]))
Leave empty cells below; #SPILL! means something is in the way
features.plain: One formula returns a whole list that grows or shrinks by itself.
features.example: =UNIQUE(Customer) lists each customer once. Add a new customer to the data and it appears in the list.
features.watch: It needs empty cells below. If something is in the way you get #SPILL!.

features.name: LET
features.what: Name parts of a long formula inside it. Easier to read and faster.
features.use: Forecast formulas that reuse the same lookup several times.
features.oldVersion: #NAME? in 2019 and older.
steps: =LET(sales, SUMIFS(…), cost, SUMIFS(…), sales-cost)
Name each part once; the last argument is the result
features.plain: Give names to parts of a long formula, so it's shorter, easier to read and faster.
features.example: =LET(s, SUM(Sales), c, SUM(Cost), (s-c)/s) gives GP% without repeating SUM(Sales).
features.watch: Names can't look like cell addresses (A1, GP1). Use words like sales, cost.

features.name: LAMBDA (make your own function)
features.what: Write a formula once, save it as a name (Name Manager), use it like a built-in function.
features.use: =FYPERIOD(date) or =AGEBUCKET(days) used across every workbook the same way.
features.oldVersion: #NAME? in 2021 and older.
steps: Test first: =LAMBDA(d, MOD(MONTH(d)-4,12)+1)(A2)
Name Manager › New › Name: FYPERIOD
Refers to: =LAMBDA(d, MOD(MONTH(d)-4,12)+1)
Now use =FYPERIOD(A2) anywhere in the workbook
features.plain: Create your own Excel function once and reuse it everywhere by name.
features.example: Define FYPERIOD once. Then =FYPERIOD(A2) gives 2 for a May date, in any cell of that workbook.
features.watch: It exists only in that workbook. Copy the name to other files that need it.

features.name: GROUPBY & PIVOTBY
features.what: Pivot-style summary with a formula. Refreshes itself, no Refresh button.
features.use: Sales by customer by month that updates as soon as new rows land in the Table.
features.oldVersion: Not in any perpetual version, 2024 included.
steps: =GROUPBY(tblSales[Customer], tblSales[Amount], SUM)
=PIVOTBY(tblSales[Customer], tblSales[Month], tblSales[Amount], SUM)
Extra arguments control totals and sorting
features.plain: A pivot table made with a formula. It updates instantly, with no Refresh button.
features.example: =GROUPBY(Customer, Amount, SUM) gives each customer with their total sales.
features.watch: Only in Microsoft 365. People on Excel 2024 or older see #NAME?.

features.name: VSTACK, HSTACK, TEXTSPLIT, TAKE, DROP, CHOOSECOLS
features.what: Stack sheets, split text, take top N rows, pick columns. All with formulas.
features.use: Stack several company sheets into one list; top 10 customers by AR.
features.oldVersion: #NAME? in 2021 and older.
steps: Stack sheets: =VSTACK(CoA!A2:F500, CoB!A2:F500)
Top 10: =TAKE(SORT(tbl,3,-1),10)
Split text: =TEXTSPLIT(A2," - ")
features.plain: Tools to stack, split and trim lists with formulas instead of copy-paste.
features.example: =VSTACK(CoA!A2:D100, CoB!A2:D100) puts both companies' rows into one list.
features.watch: Blank rows in the ranges come through as zeros. Trim the ranges or filter out blanks.

features.name: REGEX functions
features.what: REGEXTEST, REGEXEXTRACT, REGEXREPLACE find patterns in text.
features.use: Extract invoice number from messy bank transaction descriptions for matching.
features.oldVersion: Not in perpetual versions.
steps: =REGEXEXTRACT(A2,"INV\d+") pulls INV12345 out of text
=REGEXTEST(A2,"^\d{10}$") checks for exactly 10 digits
Feed the result into XLOOKUP to match
features.plain: Find text that follows a pattern, like 'INV followed by numbers', inside messy text.
features.example: From 'IBG CR ABC SDN BHD INV20456 REF' → =REGEXEXTRACT(A2,"INV\d+") gives INV20456.
features.watch: Patterns are fussy. Test on a few rows before applying to all.

rows: IBG CR ABC SDN BHD INV20456 REF

features.name: PivotTable
features.what: Drag fields to summarise thousands of rows in seconds.
features.use: Trial balance by company and account group; expenses by cost centre by month.
steps: Click inside your Table › Insert › PivotTable › New Worksheet
Drag Account to Rows, Company to Columns, Amount to Values
Right-click › Refresh after the data changes
PivotTable Design › Report Layout › Show in Tabular Form
features.plain: Summarise thousands of rows into a small table by dragging fields, with no formulas.
features.example: 50,000 GL lines become a table of account × company totals in 10 seconds.
features.watch: Without Auto Refresh (see next card), it does not update by itself: right-click › Refresh after the data changes.

features.name: Auto-refresh PivotTables
features.plain: Make a PivotTable update by itself when the data changes, instead of clicking Refresh.
features.what: PivotTable Analyze › Auto Refresh keeps pivots built on data inside the same workbook up to date. Where it is not available yet, use Refresh on open, Refresh All, or the GROUPBY formula.
features.use: AR or accrual pivot that stays correct while people add rows during closing.
features.example: Change Freight in the data from 100 to 118. The pivot total shows 118 straight away, no Refresh click.
features.watch: Still rolling out: Microsoft says Insider only for now. Only works for data inside the workbook. No button? Use the steps below.

itBlocks.why: Stops company files from being forwarded to anyone on the internet.
